title: AWS Introduces Centralized Workforce Access to IAM Roles Across Accounts
summary:
AWS recently introduced Account Access Manager to centrally assign workforce users and groups to existing IAM roles across an organization, preserving custom trust policies and ABAC configurations while improving individual identity attribution and auditability.

By Renato Losio

title: Azure AI Gateway Reaches General Availability as a Standalone Service
summary:
Microsoft has made Azure AI Gateway generally available as a standalone Azure service for governing access to AI models and MCP tools across providers. A free tier covers 10,000 requests per gateway per month; paid billing starts January 1, 2027; and private networking remains in preview.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers

title: Meta Brings Code Review Auto-Approval More Mainstream with PyTorch GreenLight
summary:
PyTorch now lets an AI reviewer approve pull requests from its own maintainers. GreenLight is an open-source take on RADAR, the system Meta uses to auto-land low-risk diffs after safety checks, a risk score and an LLM review. OpenAI, Anthropic and Sonar describe similar ways to automate approval while keeping humans on risky changes.

By Andrew Hoblitzell

title: Netflix Builds Quasar to Measure the Blast Radius of Library API Changes
summary:
Netflix developed Quasar, an internal tool that combines semantic code indexing and API comparisons to identify downstream consumers affected by library changes. Using SCIP, Amazon S3, and Athena, it traces API references across repositories, helping maintainers assess migration impact and make informed release decisions. Netflix is also exploring agent-assisted consumer migrations.

By Leela Kumili

title: Presentation: From Fan-Out to Fast: Sub-100ms API Design in Distributed Systems
summary:
Saranya Vedagiri explains how to design resilient, low-latency distributed APIs under 100ms. Drawing on practical scale at eBay, she discusses hop-by-hop latency budgets, async fanout tradeoffs, thread pool sizing, caching, and circuit breakers. Learn actionable strategies to eliminate tail-latency bottlenecks and establish performance-first engineering practices.

By Saranya Vedagiri

title: Article: Engineering Reliable Telematics from Smartphone Sensors
summary:
Smartphones make telematics more accessible by combining location, motion sensors, computing power, and connectivity in a single device. But the convenience comes with a trade-off: device placement varies, sampling behavior is managed by the mobile platform, and measurements have different timing and coordinate semantics. This article explores a six-stage architecture to address these challenges.

By Praveen Kumar Gopalakrishnan

title: Mozilla Partners with Mistral to Bring Open-Weight AI Models to Firefox Smart Window
summary:
Mozilla has partnered with Mistral AI to offer Mistral Small 4, an open-weight model, in Firefox's Smart Window AI assistant, now in beta. It is recommended for users in France, the US and Canada. Users can choose among several models, and Mistral agreed to zero data retention. Beta feedback is mixed.

By Daniel Curtis

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: How to Kill the Code Review
summary:
Ankit Jain of Aviator told QCon San Francisco 2026 that line-by-line code review is already fading, since most review comments concern knowledge sharing rather than defects and over 75% of PRs merge without human review. He proposed six layers: argue, capture, codify, prove, debate, own. His team merges four times more PRs, with about 40% fewer reverts.

By Daniel Curtis

summary:
Training can act as a confidence engine, turning repeated behaviors into habits and culture. We can tailor training programs that equip developers and operators with the skills to run their services in line with the organization’s maturity and growth, and apply SRE principles to the training itself.

By Ben Linders

title: Presentation: Finetuning Your Embedding Model for Better Search: Learning from Agentic Search at Dell
summary:
Rachel Shalom explains how Dell solved enterprise RAG retrieval failures on internal terminology by fine-tuning open-source embedding models. She discusses data prep with hard negatives, distributed InfoNCE loss training on H100 GPUs, automated hyperparameter tuning, and production evaluation using LLM-as-a-judge.

By Rachel Shalom

title: .NET MAUI 11 Makes CoreCLR the Default Runtime and Adds Incremental XAML Hot Reload
summary:
Microsoft released .NET 11 with a .NET MAUI update focused on product quality. CoreCLR is now the default runtime on all platforms, and XAML gets incremental hot reload, implicit namespaces and faster resource dictionaries. The release also adds device test templates and passkey support, and raises the minimum Android and Apple platform versions.

By Edin Kapić

title: Mock Service Worker Releases v3.0 with ESM-Only Build, Socket-Based Interception and GraphQL Subs
summary:
Mock Service Worker 3.0 is now ESM-only, requires Node.js 22 or later, and cuts package size from 416KB to 234KB. It adds GraphQL subscription support, protocol-specific entrypoints, and an experimental defineNetwork API. Node.js interception now works at the TCP and TLS level. Some users report test failures from newly intercepted OPTIONS preflight requests.

By Daniel Curtis
